data.summary: added: Preprint: Wealth inequalities malaria parasitaemia and child anaemia in Nigeria

after.title: Preprint: Wealth inequalities malaria parasitaemia and child anaemia in Nigeria
after.authors: Fowobaje, K. R.; Adegbenro, A.; Lawson, T.
after.abstract: Anaemia and malaria remain concentrated among children living in poorer households in Nigeria, but the extent to which the wealth gradient in anaemia operates through current malaria parasitaemia is uncertain. We used three nationally representative surveys to estimate a clearly defined parasitaemia-mediated component of the association, while recognising that anaemia has multiple infectious, nutritional, genetic, and social causes. We analysed de facto children aged 6-59 months in the 2010, 2015, and 2021 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Surveys. Within each survey, we contrasted children in the poorest quintile with children in the richer and richest quintiles. The outcome was altitude-adjusted anaemia and the mediator was microscopy-confirmed parasitaemia. Weighted outcome and mediator models adjusted for child age and sex, maternal education, urban residence, geopolitical zone, household size, rainy-season interview, and altitude. We standardized interventional total, direct, and indirect effects using g-computation. Missing data were addressed with 20 chained-equation imputations; uncertainty used 1,000 Rao-Wu survey-bootstrap replicates. Analytic samples included 3,307, 3,643, and 6,572 children in 2010, 2015, and 2021. The multiple-imputation total risk difference was 11.0 (95% CI 4.1 to 17.9) percentage points in 2015 and 12.5 (95% CI 8.4 to 16.6) points in 2021; corresponding parasitaemia-mediated indirect differences were 3.4 (95% CI 1.4 to 5.4) and 2.0 (95% CI 1.1 to 2.9) points. The 2010 total-effect interval included zero. Proportion-mediated estimates were withheld for 2010 and 2015 because of unstable total-effect denominators. The poorest-to-richer/richest contrast was associated with higher anaemia risk in 2015 and 2021. A smaller positive component was compatible with mediation through microscopy-confirmed parasitaemia. Because wealth, parasitaemia, and haemoglobin were measured in the same survey visit, the estimates require assumptions about temporal ordering and unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding; they do not establish that eliminating parasitaemia would remove the observed anaemia inequality.

after.title: Preprint: Implementing community-based minimally invasive tissue sampling for mortality surveillance in rural South Africa: A process evaluation of the Vukamberi project
after.authors: Mondlane, Z. L.; Kahn, K.; Chipungu, S.; Wagner, R. G.; Tippett Barr, B.; Price, J.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of the Witwatersrand Faculty of Health Sciences
after.abstract: Accurate cause-of-death data are limited in rural low- and middle-income settings, where most deaths occur at home without medical certification. Minimally invasive tissue sampling (MITS) is a culturally acceptable alternative to complete autopsy but has largely been applied to stillbirths and child deaths. We evaluated the process and implementation of a community-based, all-age MITS study in rural South Africa. The Vukamberi project ("to examine" in Xitsonga) is a prospective study in rural Bushbuckridge sub-district, Mpumalanga Province. Guided by the Medical Research Council Framework for Complex Interventions and Proctors Implementation Outcomes Framework, we assessed reach, adoption, fidelity, feasibility, acceptability and timeliness using prospectively collected records of deaths notified between 07 July 2024 to 30 June 2026, and mapped challenges to adaptive strategies by domain and phase. All 408 notified community deaths were screened, and 316 (77.5%) were eligible. Families consented for 206 eligible cases (65.2%), all of which proceeded to MITS, with target-organ sampling adherence in 199 (96.6%). Median time from death to notification was 15 hours (interquartile range [IQR] 5-23) and to MITS completion 37 hours (IQR 25-49). Enrolled decedents were 197 adults (95.6%) and 9 paediatric cases (4.4%). Main ineligibility reasons were in-hospital death (excluded by design; 27 cases) and notification beyond 48 hours (26 cases). Family refusal, mostly reflecting grief-related unreadiness and sociocultural barriers, accounted for 53 (48.2%) non-enrolled eligible cases. Adaptive strategies that increased enrolment included extending recruitment beyond the Agincourt Health and Socio-Demographic Surveillance System into the wider sub-district, incentivised community informants, elder-mediated consent, gender-appropriate field staff, non-disfigurement messaging in local languages and mortuary-based consenting where household access was restricted by a traditional leader. Community-based MITS was feasible in this rural setting. Culturally responsive consent strategies, mortuary partnerships and multi-channel death notification helped overcome sociocultural and logistical barriers, and a reliable supply of consumables proved essential for continuous enrolment. These findings may inform community-based mortality surveillance in other low- and middle-income settings.

Adaptive strategies that increased enrolment included extending recruitment beyond the Agincourt Health and Socio-Demographic Surveillance System into the wider sub-district, incentivised community informants, elder-mediated consent, gender-appropriate field staff, non-disfigurement messaging in local languages and mortuary-based consenting where household access was restricted by a traditional leader. Community-based MITS was feasible in this rural setting. Culturally responsive consent strategies, mortuary partnerships and multi-channel death notification helped overcome sociocultural and logistical barriers, and a reliable supply of consumables proved essential for continuous enrolment. These findings may inform community-based mortality surveillance in other low- and middle-income settings.

after.title: Preprint: MLX-Radiomics: accelerating standardized regional and voxel-wise radiomics for CT, PET and MRI
after.authors: Sandoval, J.; Sandoval, A.; Saleem, A.
after.abstract: Background: Differences among radiomics implementations complicate cross-study comparisons, while voxel-wise feature extraction remains computationally demanding. We developed MLX-Radiomics to accelerate regional feature extraction and voxel-wise mapping while preserving agreement with standardized reference measurements. Methods: MLX-Radiomics implements 172 feature definitions from the Image Biomarker Standardization Initiative (IBSI), 16 extensions and the IBSI 2 image filters. We assessed agreement with IBSI reference data and evaluated numerical accuracy against independent double-precision and analytic calculations. In matched comparisons on Apple M1 Max and M5 Max systems, we used the IBSI reference CT to compare feature values, extraction time and memory use with PyRadiomics, MIRP and Flash-Radiomics, and feature values with FastRad. Separately, we compared the time required to generate voxel-wise feature maps for regions of up to 10.1 million voxels with published GPU results obtained on different hardware and images. We evaluated agreement with MIRP under published settings in a 51-patient cohort with CT, FDG PET and T1-weighted MRI. Results: MLX-Radiomics agreed with all 2,160 IBSI reference measurements within the specified tolerances. With matching outputs, MLX-Radiomics was 2.66 to 7.27 times faster than PyRadiomics and MIRP for regional feature extraction and 198 to 218 times faster than PyRadiomics for voxel-wise mapping on a 24 x 24 x 24-voxel crop. It also outperformed the fastest Flash-Radiomics CPU configurations tested. On the M5 Max, generating 93 maps over 10.1 million voxels took 23.8 s. In the patient cohort, MLX-Radiomics and MIRP agreed on 98.0% of requested values. For tumors at the image edge, matching the libraries' resampling rules substantially improved agreement. Conclusions: MLX-Radiomics provides standardized regional measurements and voxel-wise maps for CT, PET and MRI, with evidence of faster extraction limited to CT. It can support quantitative imaging research on relatively inexpensive hardware without requiring a separate GPU workstation.

after.abstract: Spine Endoscopic Atlas-Tissue (SEA-T) is a multicenter dataset for pixel-level multi-class semantic segmentation in endoscopic spine surgery. It contains 3,310 expert-annotated frames from 65 patients (1,663 cervical frames from 39 patients; 1,647 lumbar frames from 26 patients) across three centers, plus 11,155 unlabeled frames. Annotations cover nine classes - upper/lower lamina, ligamentum flavum, dural sac, nerve root, adipose tissue, muscle, disc material, and instrument channel - created in 3D Slicer under multi-stage quality control, with Fleiss' kappa of 0.789. The annotated data are split by center, procedure, and anatomy into Center A training, internal validation, internal test, and held-out sub-cohorts, with Center B and Center C external tests; unlabeled frames are kept separate. Baselines spanning convolutional and foundation-model paradigms - nnU-Net v2, CaraNet, MedSAM2, and the SAM-based MA-SAM baseline - report Dice-based evaluation and reveal center-dependent domain shift. SEA-T is released with native-resolution PNG images, NRRD/MRML masks, RGB overlay images for annotation review, and metadata.

after.title: Preprint: The effects of exercise and physical activity on gait biomechanics and pain in knee osteoarthritis: A systematic review and meta-analysis
after.authors: Bytheway, N.; Amor, S.; Swinton, P.; Cheah, K.; Morrison, A.; Samvelyan, H. J.
after.abstract: Objectives To evaluate the effects of exercise and physical activity on gait biomechanics and pain in adults with knee osteoarthritis. Methods Systematic searches were performed of PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus and SPORTDiscus databases for controlled intervention studies published up to 31 December 2024. Eligible studies included adults with knee osteoarthritis undertaking exercise or physical activity compared with control group(s). Risk of bias was assessed using the Downs and Black Checklist. Bayesian three-level hierarchical random-effects meta-analyses synthesised standardised mean differences (SMD; effect size) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). Results Of 2,602 records identified, 18 studies involving 1,102 participants (345 males and 757 females) were included. Exercise and physical activity reduced pain (SMD 0.61, 95% CrI 0.29 to 0.92) and improved spatiotemporal gait parameters (SMD 0.67, 95% CrI 0.27 to 1.05). Improvements were reported across several intervention types, including strengthening, aerobic, multicomponent, and mind-body exercise. Effects on knee kinematics (SMD 0.12, 95% CrI -0.18 to 0.41) and kinetics (SMD -0.03, 95% CrI -0.25 to 0.18) were small or uncertain. Conclusions Exercise and physical activity may improve pain and spatiotemporal gait characteristics in knee osteoarthritis, but consistent improvements in knee kinematics and kinetics were not demonstrated. Further adequately powered trials with standardised biomechanical assessments and longer assessments are needed.

after.title: Preprint: User-Informed Design of a Psychological Support Social Pet Robot for Community-Dwelling People With Long-Term Physical Disabilities: A Formative Study
after.authors: Lu, Y.; Chen, X.; Hui, R.; Dai, Y.; Mei, X.; So, H.; Li, C.; Tao, X.; Li, Y.
after.author_corresponding_institution: School of Nursing, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University
after.abstract: Background. Community-dwelling people with long-term physical disabilities may experience pain that interferes with daily and social activities and is associated with poorer mental wellbeing. A home-based psychological support social pet robot could offer mood check-ins, companionship, supportive interaction, and mindfulness guidance for community-dwelling people with long-term physical disabilities. Preliminary evidence is needed to understand their preferences and translate them into candidate design requirements. Objective. This study aimed to identify preliminary needs and preferences to inform a psychological support social pet robot for community-dwelling people with long-term physical disabilities, offering mood check-ins, companionship, and mindfulness guidance at home. Methods. We conducted a 3-phase formative user-informed design study comprising initial concept development, qualitative target user interviews, and a design workshop. Six community-dwelling adults with long-term physical disabilities took part in the interviews, and one participant also answered the workshop questions by telephone. Four authors used modified workshop materials to synthesize the interview findings and separate responses into an early product plan. Results. Qualitative content analysis of the interview transcripts produced 5 themes. These were emotional support, soft touch and appearance, mindfulness delivery, context of use, and ease of use and accessibility. Participants expressed preferences about companionship, touch, use settings, and interaction effort. The author workshop combined these findings with author and technical judgments to develop candidate requirements for dialogue and mindfulness delivery. The resulting psychological support concept combined mood check-ins and companion-oriented interaction with flexible mindfulness guidance. The design also needed to consider pain and daily routines. After the workshop, the authors developed a physical proof-of-concept prototype. It implemented only part of the candidate requirements and included additional author or technical choices. Conclusions. For this small community-dwelling sample, target user input showed that home use, physical access, companionship, and flexible support were important. Mindfulness was one component of the broader psychological support role, alongside mood check-ins and optional companion interaction. The prototype illustrates but does not validate the early requirements. Further studies should include people with a wider range of long-term physical disabilities and test usability, accessibility, privacy, and nursing value. Keywords. social pet robots; user-informed design; psychological support; mindfulness; long-term physical disabilities; community dwelling; user centered design; human robot interaction; mental health; qualitative research

after.authors: Ringo, F. S.; M, U. M.; R, B.; S, M.; H, M.; A, J.; A, Z. M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences
after.abstract: ABSTRACT Maternal ICU admission provides advanced, lifesaving medical care for pregnant or postpartum women who are critically ill. The burden of obstetric critical illness requiring ICU admission is higher in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) than in high-income countries. Most critically ill obstetric patients admitted to the ICU have undergone major surgical interventions such as caesarean sections, hysterectomies and explorative laparotomies. Common indications for maternal ICU admission following surgery include postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and sepsis. Maternal ICU admission following obstetric surgery is associated with high maternal mortality, prolonged ICU stay, and poor neonatal outcomes. Identifying factors associated with poor maternal outcomes after ICU admission following obstetrics surgeries is essential for reducing preventable severe morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to assess the factors associated with the clinical outcomes of maternal ICU admissions following obstetric surgery at Muhimbili National Hospital (MNH), Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. This was a prospective cross-sectional study, conducted at the MNH, Obstetrics ICU, involving 115 women admitted following obstetric surgery. Data were collected using a modified WHO maternal near-miss checklist. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 27. Categorical variables were summarized using frequencies and percentages, and continuous variables were summarized using median and interquartile range (IQR). The associations between variables were assessed using Pearsons chi-square and Fishers exact tests. Modified Poisson regression analysis was used to determine the strength of associations, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05 and 95% confidence interval. PPH was the most common indication for maternal ICU admission following surgery, accounting for 46.1% of admissions. The overall maternal ICU mortality was 16.5%, whereas 40.9% of patients experienced prolonged ICU stays. In bivariate analysis, mechanical ventilation (p = 0.04) and use of inotropes and/or vasopressors (p = 0.022) were significantly associated with maternal mortality, while mechanical ventilation (p = 0.025), PPH (p = 0.031), and blood and/or blood products transfusion (p = 0.003) were significantly associated with prolonged ICU stay. In the modified Poisson regression analysis, mechanical ventilation (adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR] = 2.3; 95% CI: 1.11-4.64; p = 0.025) and blood and/or blood product transfusion (aPR = 1.9; 95% CI: 1.23-2.80; p = 0.003) were independently and significantly associated with prolonged ICU stay. This study demonstrates that PPH was the most common indication for maternal ICU admission following obstetric surgery. The overall maternal mortality was 16.5% with 40.9% of patients experience prolonged ICU stay. The need for mechanical ventilation, vasoactive support and blood transfusion were significantly associated with poor maternal outcomes. Healthcare providers should strengthen antenatal identification and correction of risk factors for PPH, including anaemia, previous PPH, multiple pregnancy, and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy during antenatal care visits (ANC); ensure appropriate prophylactic uterotonics administration during delivery; and promote early detection and timely, multidisciplinary management of PPH to reduce severe maternal morbidity, ICU admission, and maternal mortality. In addition, hospital management should strengthen early recognition and timely management of critically ill obstetric patients to reduce maternal mortality and prolonged ICU stay.

after.title: Preprint: Benchmarking Large Language AI Models Against Human Doctors Using an Emergency Medicine Simulation Approach
after.authors: Shahabian, M.; Hadizadeh Esfahani, A.; Ahmadi, M.; Rajabzadeh, S.; Givechin Ghamsari, M. H.; Tabaraee, A.; Hejripour Rafsanjani, S. Z.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Emergency Medicine Department, School of Medicine, AJA University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran
after.abstract: Background: Proper adoption of AI in emergency medicine necessitate thorough and rigorous appraisal. Classic benchmarks, which rely heavily on basic question-and-answer formats, though dominating the benchmarking field of LLM usage in medicine, have proven inadequate in assessing the full spectrum of skills incumbent upon an agent in healthcare. Methods: We propose an intricate benchmarking scheme in which the skill set required of an emergency physician is tested and quantified. Our benchmarking structure is 3-fold: skills such as history taking, diagnostic accuracy, treatment plan, and empathy are evaluated by an emergency medicine expert, while the same expertise is scored by an intern from the perspective of a patient, through what we call a simulated emergency room visit. A comprehensive written examination is also utilized to measure general emergency medicine knowledge. Results: Eight LLMs were benchmarked against each other and in contrast to nine emergency medical doctors. Our findings indicate that the AI models significantly outperformed human physicians across several key domains, including history taking, investigation, diagnostic accuracy, and treatment planning. Furthermore, the models demonstrated superior performance in comprehensibility, credibility, and empathy. When comparing AI models against each other, performance advantages were marginal during simulated emergency room visits and were mostly pronounced during the written examination. Conclusion: AI models demonstrate a clear advantage over human physicians across a diverse range of emergency medicine competencies. The proposed benchmarking scheme provides a comprehensive metric for a thorough evaluation of medical skill set, furthering validation, adaptation, and utilization of AI in emergency medicine.

after.authors: Robles Fontan, M. M.; Krishna, B.; Mahajan, A.; Meade, R. D.; Tiwari, A.; Balsari, S.; Buckee, C.; Irizarry, R. A.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Department of Data Science; Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, Department of Biostatistics
after.abstract: Background: Extreme heat is an increasingly pressing public health threat, particularly in South Asia. Yet the temperatures at which mortality risk begins to increase in Indian cities remain poorly characterized. Operational heat wave definitions are based on meteorological criteria and may not reflect epidemiologically relevant temperature thresholds. Widely used distributed lag non-linear models are designed to flexibly estimate expected mortality as a function of temperature, but do not directly target the onset of excess risk from heat, a quantity central to early warning and planning. Methods: We conducted a multi-city time-series study of daily mortality and temperature data in Ahmedabad (2001-2010), Chennai (2012-2017), Delhi (2011-2015), Kolkata (2011-2018), and Mumbai (2011-2015). We developed a data-driven structured modeling framework that permits likelihood-based inference for city-specific temperatures at which heat-related mortality first exceeds seasonal background levels, a parameter that is challenging to estimate and perform statistical inference from short and noisy series. Using these health-based thresholds, we also estimated heat-associated excess deaths. Results: In all five cities, the onset of excess mortality occurred at temperatures substantially lower than those implied by current operational heat wave definitions. The proposed framework yielded stable and interpretable threshold estimates and confidence intervals across heterogeneous climates and time-series lengths and identified a larger burden of heat-associated mortality than would be captured using standard meteorological criteria. Conclusions: Data-driven estimation of mortality-based heat thresholds provides epidemiologi- cally relevant targets for early warning systems and heat action plans. Reliance on meteorological definitions alone may delay intervention and underestimate population risk in rapidly warming regions.
after.summary: Background: Extreme heat is an increasingly pressing public health threat, particularly in South Asia. Widely used distributed lag non-linear models are designed to flexibly estimate expected mortality as a function of temperature, but do not directly target the onset of excess risk from heat, a quantity central to early warning and planning. Using these health-based thresholds, we also estimated heat-associated excess deaths. Results: In all five cities, the onset of excess mortality occurred at temperatures substantially lower than those implied by current operational heat wave definitions. after.abstract: Abstract: Lumbar puncture (LP) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis are essential for the diagnosis and management of central nervous system (CNS) infections, but LP is underutilised in pediatric patients in high burden settings. As part of the pre-screening and screening procedures of the SURE+DP diagnostic sub-study of the SURE pediatric tuberculous meningitis randomised control trial we identified this as a key clinical issue and quantified how often pediatric lumbar puncture was performed at recruiting African hospitals and implemented a package of interventions to increase LP rates. Methods: We evaluated the frequency of pediatric CSF sampling of children aged 28 days to 18 years at four urban tertiary hospitals in Kampala, Lusaka and Harare. We developed a family-facing educational video to support LP consent discussions. In Zambia and Zimbabwe, healthcare workers received training sessions including mannequin-based LP simulation, with knowledge, confidence, experience and perceived barriers assessed before and after training. We assessed the effect of healthcare worker LP training on confidence and LP performance and explored reported barriers to pediatric LP. Results: Median weekly pediatric CSF samples were 1 at both Sally Mugabe and Parirenyatwa hospitals in Harare, 6 at University Teaching Hospital in Lusaka, and 4 at Mulago Hospital in Kampala. Training significantly improved healthcare-worker self-reported confidence to assist (p-value <0.001) and perform pediatric LP (p-value <0.001). At the Zambian site, the proportion of children with coded diagnoses compatible with consideration of LP who had CSF samples increased by 7% in the six months after training compared with the preceding six months (p=0.002). In Zimbabwe, there was an increase in LP activity the week following training, which was not subsequently sustained. Healthcare workers identified parental refusal, limited procedural confidence, delays obtaining consent from male family decision makers, fear of complications, and consumables availability as barriers. Discussion: Pediatric LP was performed infrequently across these tertiary hospitals, and improved healthcare worker confidence following training did not consistently translate into sustained increases in LP performance. Multifaceted sustained approaches combining healthcare worker training with caregiver engagement, system level support and improved resources are needed to improve diagnostic LP use for children with suspected CNS infections.

after.abstract: Introduction. Gabapentinoid-induced peripheral edema may be misinterpreted as a new condition and treated with a loop diuretic, creating a prescribing cascade. Objective. To synthesize evidence on the gabapentinoid-to-loop diuretic prescribing cascade in adults: its magnitude, dose- and drug-related gradients, timing, and downstream harms. Methods. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science to 23 April 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261379968) for studies of loop diuretic initiation after gabapentinoid initiation and assessed risk of bias with ROBINS-I. Findings were synthesized by study design, and adjusted sequence ratios were pooled in a random-effects meta-analysis. Results. Nine studies from five countries (>1.8 million new gabapentinoid users) were included: five sequence symmetry analyses, three cohort studies, and one chart review; six were restricted to older adults and two were available only as conference reports. All five sequence symmetry analyses and both cohort studies with an unexposed comparison group found more diuretic prescribing after gabapentinoid initiation. Sequence ratios ranged from 1.23 to 1.69, with a pooled adjusted sequence ratio of 1.37 (95% CI 1.14-1.64; I2= 96%; five estimates from four studies). Both of these cohort studies reported an adjusted hazard ratio of 1.44 (loop diuretics in one, any diuretic in the other). Higher doses were associated with larger estimates in four of the five studies that examined dose. In one chart review, 23.3% of patients had a potential harm within 60 days of starting a loop diuretic. Conclusions. Gabapentinoid initiation was associated with subsequent loop diuretic prescribing, mainly in older adults, consistent with a prescribing cascade. Clinicians may consider a recently started gabapentinoid as a possible cause of new edema before adding a loop diuretic.

after.abstract: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) is characterized by a severe pattern of symptoms including emotional instability, impulsivity, and unstable interpersonal relationships. A complex interplay between genetics and environmental factors has been hypothesized to be associated with the development of BPD. While neuroimaging studies have identified structural and functional changes in the brain, and genome-wide association studies described some first genetic risk loci, the neurobiological underpinnings of BPD remain poorly described. To better understand disease processes in BPD, we performed a molecular characterization of the prefrontal cortex (PFC), an important brain region for emotion and impulsivity regulation in BPD. Label-free brain proteomics was performed in postmortem human brain tissue in a sample of n=79, with a case group of n=36 individuals with BPD and a control group of n=43 individuals without BPD. Differential protein expression analysis suggested protein-level dysregulation of mitochondrial, immunological, and neuroplasticity pathways. Network analyses identified a BPD-associated co-expression module enriched for protein secretory and synaptic processes that is druggable with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors. Additional druggability analyses on protein-protein interaction networks and drug-repositioning analysis suggested VEGF signaling as a potential pharmacologic target in BPD. When we integrated BPD proteomic signatures with genomic and proteomic datasets of common comorbidities such as posttraumatic stress disorder and major depressive disorder, we observed a strong convergent overlap across disorders, with STX7 and RTN4 identified as conserved, differentially expressed proteins. Our study provides first insights into proteomic signatures of BPD in the brain, suggests potential pharmacological targets, and provides evidence for convergent protein signatures across BPD and common comorbidites.

after.authors: Jensen, L. W. H.; Johansen, S. K.; Lyng, K. D.; Rahbek, O.; Kold, S.
after.abstract: Introduction Caregivers of children with disabilities act as intermediaries between professionals due to fragmented communication and information sharing across sectors. The use of shared digital communication may support integrated care. Therefore, this study explored challenges and needs among caregivers and professionals and how an existing shared digital communication intervention could be adapted to support communication and coordination in this context. Methods Three future workshops involved 26 co-designers: caregivers (n=8), professionals across sectors (n=14), and software developers (n=4). Caregiver and professional data were analysed thematically, followed by matrix analysis to identify convergences, tensions, and design principles. In workshop with software developers, design principles were translated into design specifications. Results Both caregivers and professionals described how caregivers become de facto care coordinators. Clear responsibilities, continuity, and shared knowledge were identified as essential for improving communication and coordination. Shared digital communication was considered promising, but tensions emerged between accessibility and workload, and between transparency and confidentiality. The adapted intervention incorporated structured communication, shared responsibility, relational continuity, a shared overview, and a human digital coordination function. Discussion/conclusion The adapted intervention provides a foundation for cross-sector communication between caregivers and professionals and adds to the evidence base of communication solutions that may strengthen integrated care.

after.abstract: Gentrification is a global, accelerating urban process involving complex socio-spatial transformations. Although increasingly recognised as a determinant of urban health, quantitative evidence on its population health impacts remains scarce and inconsistent, limiting evidence-informed urban policymaking, especially in rapidly gentrifying contexts. Thus, we assessed the health impact of neighbourhood-level gentrification among adults in Porto (Northern Portugal), a hotspot of transnational gentrification. A quasi-experimental study was conducted using data from the EPIPorto population-based cohort (1999-2022), with 2,485 participants at baseline. A validated, context-sensitive 16-variable index of transnational gentrification, derived from 2011 and 2021 census and tourism-accommodation data through Principal Component Analysis, enabled neighbourhood classification as gentrifying or non-gentrifying. Difference-in-differences models estimated the effect of living in gentrifying neighbourhoods on ten cardiometabolic and behavioural outcomes. Inverse probability of censoring weighting was used to account for loss to follow-up and missing data. At baseline, 26.2% of participants resided in gentrifying neighbourhoods. Residence in a gentrifying neighbourhood was associated with a statistically significant reduction in nightly sleep duration (-0.346 h; 95% CI -0.650, -0.042), with statistically significant reductions in the lower-education and [≥]65-year subgroups. No significant effects were observed for body mass index, overweight/obesity, total/HDL/LDL cholesterol, blood pressure, and tobacco or alcohol use. Transnational gentrification in Porto showed limited effects on most cardiometabolic outcomes but was associated with reduced sleep duration, suggesting that the health impacts of gentrification may initially emerge through psychosocial pathways before translating into measurable cardiometabolic changes.

after.authors: Ni Chobhthaigh, S.; Cox, C.; Greenway-Bailey, T.; Musanu, J.; Green, M.; Buhari, A.; Mawi, M.; Neave, C.; Burgess, R. A.; Jay, M. A.; Devakumar, D.

after.abstract: Background. Unmet mental health and education needs increase the risk of youth justice contact. Understanding inequalities in alternative provision (AP) and how these relate to school recorded mental health needs or police criminalisation may identify opportunities to intervene. Methods. We analysed population-level linked school and police administrative data for 3.7m pupils (born 1997-2003) who attended state schools in England. We examined differences by racial-ethnic group and gender in rates and timing of AP enrolment and recording patterns of mental health-related provision and youth justice contacts among pupils with AP enrolment. Results. Our findings indicate heightened mental health need and vulnerability to criminalisation among pupils recorded with AP enrolment. Enrolment was highest among Irish Traveller and Romani pupils, followed by Black Caribbean and Mixed White-Black Caribbean pupils. Boys were enrolled more than girls, but some girls had higher rates than boys from other groups. Over 50% boys from Black Caribbean and Mixed White-Black Caribbean backgrounds with AP enrolment had a youth justice contact, the majority of whom had recorded mental health needs. Conclusion. Heightened need and intersectional inequalities among pupils enrolled in AP highlight the importance of a co-ordinated public health approach to understanding and responding to children's needs.

after.abstract: Objective To examine temporal trends in in-hospital mortality among patients hospitalized with heart failure, ischemic heart disease, and cerebrovascular disease in Suriname from 2013 to 2022, and to assess differences according to age, sex, and ethnicity. Methods Conducted a retrospective hospital-based observational study using routinely collected discharge data from three major public hospitals in Suriname. These hospitals accounted for approximately 71.8% of national hospital admissions. Admissions with a primary diagnosis of HF (ICD-10 I50), IHD (I20-I25), or Stroke (I60-I69) were included. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were fitted for each disease, adjusting for calendar year, age, sex, and ethnicity. Results Among 84,691 admissions, 42,301 were IHD, 24,584 for Stroke, and 17,806 for HF. In-hospital mortality declined significantly across all three conditions, with adjusted odds decreasing by 14% annually for HF (aOR 0.858; 95% CI 0.841-0.875), 6% for IHD (aOR 0.941; 95% CI 0.914-0.969), and 5% for Stroke (aOR 0.947; 95% CI 0.931-0.963). Increasing age was associated with higher mortality in IHD and Stroke. Female sex was associated with lower mortality in HF (aOR 0.835; 95% CI 0.744-0.937). Ethnic disparities were most pronounced for Stroke, with higher mortality among Maroon, Creole, Javanese, and Other groups than Hindustani patients. Conclusions In-hospital mortality declined across cardiovascular conditions, but improvements were heterogeneous. Pronounced ethnic inequalities in Stroke mortality and age-related gradients highlight the need for equity-focused cardiovascular surveillance and provide a baseline for evaluating future health-system and prevention initiatives in Suriname.

Ethnic disparities were most pronounced for Stroke, with higher mortality among Maroon, Creole, Javanese, and Other groups than Hindustani patients. Conclusions In-hospital mortality declined across cardiovascular conditions, but improvements were heterogeneous. Pronounced ethnic inequalities in Stroke mortality and age-related gradients highlight the need for equity-focused cardiovascular surveillance and provide a baseline for evaluating future health-system and prevention initiatives in Suriname.

after.abstract: Background: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease associated with the destruction of cartilage and bone, increased risk of cardiovascular disease and a higher mortality rate. Despite the many therapies that exist for RA, there is little information to guide selection of the most effective treatment for an individual patient. Ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies have created an opportunity to investigate the target tissue. While a number of studies have characterized the stromal and immune cell populations using single-cell technology on synovial biopsy samples, here we performed a longitudinal study, where we collected comprehensive clinical data over a one-year period on each patient in the process of changing their therapy. Methods: Samples from minimally invasive, ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies were collected from RA patients at baseline prior to start of a new therapy and 4-6-week follow-up under IRB-approved protocols with informed consent. Comprehensive clinical data from each appointment were recorded into a shared REDCap database. Failure to respond to therapy was based on clinical disease activity index (CDAI) for RA after 12-18 weeks post therapy. Biopsied samples were dissociated, enriched for CD45 or CD45CD11b cells, and processed on the 10X Genomics Chromium platform to generate libraries for single-cell RNA sequencing with cell-surface protein detection (CITE-seq). Spatial transcriptomics were performed on formalin-fixed paraffin embedded sections analyzed with 10X Xenium and NanoString CosMx. Results: We performed CITE-seq analysis on ~38,000 CD45+ synovial cells isolated from 17 patients who failed a conventional or biologic DMARD and planned to change therapy. We then subclustered on the myeloid population to reveal 12 myeloid subpopulations that consist of macrophages (n = 8), Osteoclast-like cells, DCs (n = 2) and proliferating cells. The proportion of cDCs was significantly higher in responders, while the proportion of macrophages was significantly lower in responders. The proportion of ISG15+ and THBS1+macrophages were enriched in the non-responder patients. Spatial transcriptomics revealed that ISG15+ macrophages were preferentially localized to the synovial lining, while the THBS1+ macrophages are likely interacting with lymphoid cells within the sublining tissue. Conclusions: These data are among the first to prospectively profile macrophage populations as predictors of response to therapy. Future studies are required to verify whether myeloid subpopulation associations hold across specific therapies.

after.abstract: Human preimplantation embryos express the SARS-CoV-2 entry factors ACE2, TMPRSS2 and BSG (CD147) on trophectoderm (TE) cells, suggesting susceptibility to infection. Likewise, SARS-CoV-2-pseudotyped reporter viruses induced cytopathic effects in blastocysts, while the zona pellucida (ZP) appeared to confer partial protection. The impact of authentic SARS-CoV-2 infection on embryonic lineage specification and developmental competence has not been established. Here, we exposed cryopreserved human embryos, donated under ethics approval and informed consent, to authentic SARS-CoV-2 (B.1.617.2, Delta variant). While embryos with an intact ZP remained uninfected, laser-assisted hatching rendered 19/21 (90.5%) of embryos susceptible to infection, as confirmed by detection of viral dsRNA. Moreover, SARS-CoV-2 infection had a pronounced effect on blastocyst development with a possibly fatal outcome. Compared to mock-treated embryos (n = 47), infected blastocysts (n = 48) showed a significantly reduced surface area (p = 0.0003), reduced total cell number (p = 0.0139), and reduced NANOG+ epiblast cell numbers (p = 0.0054) 24 hours post-exposure, while the number of GATA4+ primitive endoderm cells remained unaffected (p = 0.5255). Intriguingly, despite viral replication being largely confined to the trophectoderm (TE), this selective epiblast reduction suggests a disruption of TE-derived paracrine signaling required for epiblast specification. Finally, prolonged viral replication resulted in embryonic lysis and death. Digital transcriptomic profiling (mock, n = 29 embryos; SARS-CoV-2, n = 28 embryos; each in n = 5 minipools) revealed upregulation of innate antiviral and inflammatory genes, including IFIH1, IRF7, NOD2, and TNFRSF1A, as well as the recently identified SARS-CoV-2 entry factor TMEM106B, alongside altered developmental signatures concerning genome activation, pluripotency, and lineage-specific programs. These findings show that ZP disruption makes human blastocysts susceptible to productive SARS-CoV-2 infection, with adverse consequences for lineage allocation and direct implications for biosafety and virological counselling in medically assisted reproduction practice.

after.author_corresponding_institution: Ningbo No.2 Hospital, Ningbo Institue of Life and Health Industry, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
after.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Advanced glycation end products accumulate in Alzheimer's disease (AD) brain, but the clinical significance of circulating N{varepsilon}-(carboxymethyl)lysine (CML) remains uncertain. We evaluated serum CML as a complementary peripheral biomarker of AD. METHODS: This observational case-control study enrolled 101 patients with clinically diagnosed AD and 91 healthy controls. Serum CML was quantified in 191 participants. Multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses assessed association and discrimination. A randomly selected subcohort underwent ultrasensitive measurement of amyloid-, tau-, glial-, and neuroaxonal-related biomarkers. RESULTS: Serum CML was lower in AD than controls (median 15.26 versus 23.72 ng/mL; P<0.001). In a complete-case model (n=178), each 1-ng/mL increase was associated with lower odds of AD (adjusted odds ratio 0.727, 95% confidence interval 0.656-0.804). CML alone yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.883. Five-fold cross-validation yielded AUCs of 0.727 for a clinical model and 0.911 after adding CML. In the biomarker subcohort, AD showed lower A{beta}42/A{beta}40 and higher p-tau217; exploratory CML plus p-tau217 discrimination reached an AUC of 0.966 (n=60). DISCUSSION: Reduced serum CML was independently associated with clinically diagnosed AD and may reflect a systemic glycoxidative dimension complementary to canonical biomarkers. Its biological origins and clinical value require external, longitudinal, and biomarker-defined validation.

after.authors: Chen, M.; Yu, G.; Lai, X.; Gong, P.; Wang, S.; Liu, X.; Wu, Q.; Zhang, Y.; Sun, B.; Xu, S.; Yao, J.; Zhang, H.; Zhang, H.; Wu, Z.; Li, J.; Ren, Q.; Ji, T.

after.abstract: Reported performance of scalp electroencephalographic (EEG) seizure prediction is often inflated by lenient evaluation and by the vigilance-state, clock-time and admission-trend structure of monitoring data. We asked how much short-horizon warning survives a pre-specified, locked evaluation. Continuous video-EEG from 21 monitored children (1315 h) formed the development cohort. A statistical-process-control warning method, evaluated under a written protocol, detected 44% of evaluable seizures at 0.48 false alarms per hour, no better than a random predictor (51%, p = 0.86); its statistic moved three times more with vigilance state than with seizure approach. We re-designed it as a state-conditioned, directional scheme on seven global EEG features, froze it with a hash-recorded configuration and time-stamped pre-specification, and estimated its performance by nested leave-one-patient-out cross-validation: 15 of 45 seizures (33%) at 0.47 false alarms per hour, above analytic (21%, p = 0.034) and permutation chance, but a predictor using only clock time, vigilance state and days since admission reproduced most of this, and the signal was confined to the last 30 min. Applied once to two validation cohorts (a second batch from the same unit and the public CHB-MIT database; 101 evaluable seizures), the frozen scheme detected 19 seizures (19%) at 0.60 false alarms per hour against 26% chance (p = 0.96); no secondary endpoint was met, and with the child as the unit of analysis no cohort was above chance. Scalp-EEG warning should be evaluated under pre-specified rules against structured chance levels; the frozen scheme and framework are offered as a reference.

after.authors: Shi, R.; Svirsky, S. E.; Balogun, W. G.; Zeng, X.; Fedak, J. D.; Nafash, M.; Brodman, S. T.; Okonkwo, D. O.; Puccio, A. M.; Karikari, T. K.
after.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) are two common forms of neurotrauma that can present with overlapping clinical features, complicating early diagnosis and management particularly in acute and mixed-trauma settings.1 - 3 Accurate and rapid biological differentiation remains an unmet need.4 We hypothesized that brain-derived tau (BD-tau), an ultrasensitive blood-based biomarker preferentially selective for tau protein originating from the brain, would distinguish TBI from SCI. In a multi-cohort assessment of 342 patients admitted to the neuro-intensive care unit (285 with TBI, 57 with SCI), and 22 controls, baseline serum BD-tau concentrations were markedly elevated in TBI compared with SCI, discriminating between the two populations with high accuracy (area under the curve [AUC]=0.91, 95%CI 0.87-0.96). In paired serum-cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples, serum BD-tau significantly outperformed CSF BD-tau for injury-type discrimination (AUC=0.95, 95%CI 0.89-0.99 vs. 0.80, 95%CI 0.71-0.89). Baseline serum BD-tau also showed superior discrimination of TBI from SCI compared with established blood biomarkers of neurotrauma, including neurofilament light chain, glial fibrillary acidic protein, and ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (AUC=0.82, 95%CI 0.76-0.88; vs. 0.53, 95%CI 0.43-0.63; 0.67, 95%CI 0.58-0.76; 0.71, 95%CI 0.64-0.79; all DeLong p<0.001). Longitudinally, serum BD-tau remained persistently elevated in TBI, but not SCI, for up to 144 hours post-injury, with distinct temporal trajectories between injury types. Together, these findings indicate that serum BD-tau enables rapid and minimally invasive differentiation of TBI from SCI and may support early clinical decision-making, triage, and enrollment into injury-specific therapeutic trials, highlighting the potential of circulating biomarkers to improve precision diagnostics in acute neurotrauma care.

after.abstract: Background Patient understanding of heart failure (HF) self-care varies widely and is inconsistently associated with clinical outcomes. We examined knowledge acquisition and patient experiences related to structured HF education using a patient handbook. Methods and Results Between April and December 2021, 56 patients hospitalized for acute HF (mean age 74 years, 35% women, 46% HFrEF) were enrolled from 176 screened patients at a single center. A 20-item knowledge assessment was administered before and after nurse led HF education and at first outpatient follow-up. Thirty patients met criteria for knowledge improvement ([≥]5-point increase or baseline [≥]15), while 25 did not. Knowledge gaps were most evident in exercise, medication effects, salt restriction, and recognition of exacerbating factors. Patients with knowledge improvement had higher post-education scores (16 vs. 12), sustained knowledge at follow-up, higher serum albumin levels, better inpatient dietary intake. One-year mortality and HF readmission did not differ. A nested qualitative analysis of four readmitted patients identified 94 codes grouped into 9 categories, highlighting personalized symptom recording, persistent self-management challenges despite handbook use, enhanced communication with healthcare professionals, reflection on future care, and a desire for earlier HF education. Conclusions Patients who achieved higher HF knowledge scores demonstrated better nutritional status but similar one-year clinical outcomes. Qualitative findings underscore ongoing challenges in long-term HF self-care.

after.authors: Wan, P. K.-T.; Morris, T.; Forster, M.; Zhang, T.; Flynn, M.; Chamberlain, F.; Tuthill, M.; Thistlethwaite, F.; Williams, A.; Finch, W.; Lu, W.; Jiang, S.
after.abstract: Survivin (BIRC5) is broadly overexpressed in human cancers but, as a self-antigen, is subject to immune tolerance that limits spontaneous antitumour immunity. OVM-200 is a recombinant overlapping peptide vaccine spanning full-length survivin, with cathepsin S-cleavable linker sequences inserted between adjacent peptides to enhance antigen processing and presentation. OVM-200-100 was a multicentre, open-label phase 1 study conducted at 4 UK sites. The pooled 2,000-g cohort comprised 27 patients with advanced non-small cell lung, ovarian or prostate cancer, including 24 patients from phase 1b and 3 treated at this dose in phase 1a. OVM-200 was administered subcutaneously every 2 weeks for 3 initial vaccinations, with up to 8 additional doses in patients deriving clinical benefit. The primary endpoint was safety and tolerability, secondary endpoints included survivin-specific immunogenicity, and antitumour activity by RECIST v1.1 was exploratory. OVM-200-related adverse events were exclusively grade 1-2, with no treatment-related grade [≥]3 adverse events, dose-limiting toxicities, serious adverse events or deaths. A systematic literature analysis showed low spontaneous anti-survivin seroreactivity in patients with cancer. In our cohort, pretreatment tumours expressed survivin despite low baseline survivin-specific immunity. OVM-200 vaccination subsequently induced robust humoral and cellular responses, with median anti-survivin IgG titres increasing from 20 at baseline to a peak of 81,920 and median interferon-{gamma} ELISpot responses increasing from 16.7 to 504.6 spot-forming units per 10 PBMCs. Patients receiving [≥]4 vaccinations developed higher anti-survivin antibody titres and stronger T cell responses than those receiving fewer doses. Among 24 RECIST-evaluable patients, the best overall response was stable disease (SD) in 6 patients (25%). Patients with SD had significantly higher anti-survivin antibody titres than those with progressive disease (PD) (p=0.0418). after.title: Preprint: Retinopathy is more common, but age-related macular degeneration carries more visual impairment: a cross-sectional study of US adults graded from the same fundus photographs
after.authors: Tang, Y.; Guo, R.; Cheng, H.
after.abstract: Background Retinopathy and age-related macular degeneration (AMD) are the most common findings on fundus photographs of older adults, yet their frequency, correlates and visual consequences have been estimated in separate samples. We compared them in a national survey that graded both from the same images. Methods We analyzed 5593 adults aged >=40 years in the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2005-2008 with photographs gradable for both conditions. We estimated survey-weighted prevalence, fitted identically specified logistic models for retinopathy (participants with diabetes) and AMD (full sample), and compared presenting visual impairment (better-eye acuity worse than 20/40) and self-rated vision across four groups: neither condition, retinopathy only, AMD only, and both. Results Retinopathy was more prevalent than AMD (9.54% [95% confidence interval (CI) 8.52-10.56] vs 6.52% [5.54-7.50]); AMD overtook it only from age 70 years. In participants with diabetes, retinopathy was associated with HbA1c (odds ratio [OR] 1.54 per percentage point; 1.33-1.78) and male sex (1.54; 1.10-2.17). AMD was associated with age (OR 1.09 per year; 1.07-1.11) and was less common in non-Hispanic Black adults (0.48; 0.33-0.71). Presenting impairment affected 4.91% of participants with neither condition, 7.09% with retinopathy only, 14.57% with AMD only and 26.15% with both. After age adjustment, impairment remained associated with AMD only (OR 2.23; 1.54-3.23) and both conditions (4.09; 2.28-7.37) but not retinopathy only (1.32; 0.91-1.90). Neither retinopathy nor diabetes was associated with AMD. Self-rated vision agreed poorly with measured impairment (kappa = 0.15): only 12% of impaired participants rated their vision poor or very poor. Conclusions Retinopathy is the more frequent retinal finding in US adults aged >=40 years, but AMD carries more of the measured visual impairment, independently of age. Grading diabetic screening photographs for AMD, and measuring acuity rather than asking about vision, would reach more people who see poorly. Keywords Retinopathy; Diabetic retinopathy; Age-related macular degeneration; Visual impairment; Self-reported vision; Prevalence; NHANES; Cross-sectional studies

after.title: Preprint: Applications of Fairness Training in Artificial Intelligence to Ophthalmic Disease Diagnosis using External Eye Photographs
after.authors: Kostin, V.; Yoon, S.-H.; Chen, J. S.; Baek, S.; Seid, J.; Quyang, N.; Li, E.; Li, E.; Shi, M.; Wang, M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Harvard Ophthalmology AI Lab, Schepens Eye Research Institute of Massachusetts Eye and Ear, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA
after.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR), age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and glaucoma are leading causes of preventable blindness, yet whether external eye photographs carry phenotypic information about posterior segment disease remains unclear, and methods to mitigate demographic disparities in such models are largely unexplored. We developed and evaluated deep learning and vision-language models for binary classification of vision-threatening DR (VTDR), advanced AMD, and glaucoma using 40,687 external eye photographs from 9,878 patients at Massachusetts Eye and Ear. Convolutional networks (WResNet, EfficientNet), a vision transformer (ViT), and a fine-tuned vision-language model (LLaVA) were assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with fairness across sex, race, and ethnicity quantified by the equity-scaled AUC (ES-AUC). Five fairness-training strategies were applied to the best models. LLaVA achieved the highest baseline AUC for VTDR (85.4%, comparable to ViT 82.6%); advanced AMD was similar across architectures (EfficientNet 86.3%; LLaVA 84.8%; ViT 84.7%), whereas glaucoma was substantially worse (67-74%). Fairness training improved VTDR and AMD AUCs to 86.3% and 85.9% while partially mitigating demographic disparities. In summary, although AI models that rely on external eye photography to detect posterior segment disease may not yet be suitable for clinical deployment, the fairness methods demonstrated in this proof-of-concept study could be applied to other AI systems to decrease performance disparities and potentially improve model performance.

after.title: Preprint: Impact of DENV-ZIKV cross-reactivity in Southeast Asia: A modelling study in Thailand
after.authors: Shi, Y.; Senapati, A.; Huang, A. T.; Clapham, H. E.
after.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) is endemic across Southeast Asia (SEA), where a large proportion of adults have been infected. Zika virus (ZIKV) has circulated in the region for decades but the extent of transmission remains unclear. Prior infection with one virus can protect against or enhance infection with the other, but the population-level consequences are unknown. We developed an age-structured DENV-ZIKV model with nine cross-reactivity assumptions combining cross-protection and subsequent enhancement, and simulated sustained co-circulation under changing Thai demography. Through cross-reactivity, DENV strongly shaped ZIKV transmission, whereas ZIKV had little effect on DENV transmission. Under cross-protection, ZIKV transmission occurred as infrequent outbreaks without changes in long-term ZIKV burden. When prior DENV infection enhanced both ZIKV infection and symptomatic risk, this burden roughly doubled. Population ageing raised the mean age of DENV and ZIKV cases by over 20 years, more than cross-reactivity did. Simulated ZIKV case ages were closer to those reported in Thailand in 2019-2023 under enhancement of ZIKV infection and symptoms. Over half of individuals aged 15-49 years remained ZIKV-naive under all assumptions, leaving many pregnancies at risk of congenital Zika syndrome. Interpreting ZIKV case counts in SEA requires joint consideration of cross-reactivity, demographic change and case detection.

after.title: Preprint: The effect of carotid atherosclerosis and revascularization on cognition and dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
after.authors: Box, C. V. J.; Yu, Q.; Stroom, R.; Verhagen, H.; Howard, D. P. J.; Niehot, C.; Ikram, M. K.; Wolters, F. J.; Bos, D.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Epidemiology, Erasmus MC, Rotterdam, the Netherlands
after.abstract: Background: Carotid artery atherosclerosis may accelerate cognitive decline and increase dementia risk, but evidence is fragmented and inconsistent, and benefit of revascularization on cognitive outcomes uncertain. Methods: We systematically searched Medline, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register, and Google Scholar for articles published until 11 November 2024, reporting change in cognition or dementia incidence in relation to carotid artery intima-media thickness, plaque, stenosis, and revascularization procedures. We excluded studies that investigated people with dementia, lacked a reference group, or had post-intervention follow-up <30 days. We additionally included new data from the Rotterdam Study, and results from the recent CREST-2 trial. Two independent reviewers extracted study data. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed if data allowed. Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, Cochrane Risk of Bias, and ROBINS-I. Results: Of 5592 records identified, 97 studies were eligible, including 43 observational studies (N=100,326) and 54 intervention studies (N=15788, 6 randomized controlled trials). In observational studies, mostly among stroke-free individuals, intima-media thickness was associated with higher dementia risk (hazard ratio per 1-SD increase: 1.07, 95%CI 1.01-1.13; I2=24.8%; 5 studies), as was presence of 50-100% asymptomatic steno-occlusive disease (hazard ratio: 1.48, 95%CI 1.06 -2.07; I2=0.0%, 3 studies). Cognitive outcomes were too heterogeneous for meta-analysis, but 11/20 observational studies reported a significant association between carotid atherosclerosis and global cognition. In non-randomized intervention studies, carotid revascularization improved global cognition (standardized mean difference: 0.73, 95%CI 0.37 -1.09; I2=89.8%), but all studies were at high risk of bias, and heterogeneity was only partially explained by intervention type and study characteristics in meta-regression. Suggested benefit of stenting on cognition among Chinese patients (Standardized effect: 0.86 [0.57-1.16], 197 patients; and 1.09 [0.64-1.53], 90 patients, 2 trials) was not observed in the larger CREST-2 trial (Standardized effect: 0.03 [-0.09 to 0.15] and 0.02 [-0.09 to 0.14]), nor in post-hoc analyses of cognition in the ACAS trial and long-term dementia risk in ACST-1 (HR: 0.98 [0.75-1.28]). Conclusions: Carotid atherosclerosis is associated with increased risk of dementia. Current evidence does not support carotid revascularization for prevention of cognitive decline or dementia.
